103.h: 8 - al-Ashʿath ibn Qays ibn Maʿdī Karib al-Kindī * (ع)
103.t:
Ibn Muʿāwiyah ibn Jabalah ibn ʿAdī ibn Rabīʿah ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Akramīn ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Muʿāwiyah ibn Thawr ibn Murtaʿ ibn Kindah. ⟦2:37⟧
The name of Kindah was Thawr ibn ʿUfayr ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Murrah ibn Udad ibn Zayd ibn Yashjub ibn ʿArīb ibn Zayd ibn Kahlān ibn Sabaʾ ibn Yashjub ibn Yaʿrub ibn Qaḥṭān.
Ibn Saʿd related it, saying:
He was called Kindah because he was ungrateful (kanada) to his father for his favour, that is, he denied it.
The name of al-Ashʿath was Maʿdī Karib.
He always had dishevelled (ashʿath) hair, and the name prevailed over him.
He had companionship with the Prophet, and he narrated.
Narrating from him: الشعبي، وقيس بن أبي حازم، وأبو وائل.
Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī narrated from him in a mursal (مرسل) manner.
His eye was injured on the day of al-Yarmūk.
He was the greatest of ʿAlī's commanders on the day of Ṣiffīn.
منصور، والأعمش: عن أبي وائل:
Al-Ashʿath said to us: It was about me that this was revealed: “Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price ...” [Qurʾān 3:77].
I brought a case against a man before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: (Do you have proof?).
I said: No.
He said: (Then he will swear?).
I said: Then he will swear.
So he said: (Whoever swears a false oath in order to take away property by it will meet Allah while He is angry with him) (1).
Ibn al-Kalbī said: al-Ashʿath came as part of a delegation with seventy men of Kindah to the Prophet ﷺ.
مجالد: عن الشعبي، عن الأشعث، قال:
I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ⟦2:38⟧ with the delegation of Kindah, and he said to me: (Do you have a child?).
I said: A small one, born at the time of my setting out to you ... , the hadith (1).
And from Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, who said:
Al-Ashʿath apostatized along with some people of Kindah, and was besieged and taken under a guarantee of safety. He obtained the guarantee for seventy but did not take it for himself, and was brought to al-Ṣiddīq, who said: We are going to kill you; there is no guarantee of safety for you.
He said: Show me favour and I will become Muslim?
He said: So he did, and married him to his sister.
Another narrator added: He said to Abū Bakr: Marry me to your sister.
So he married him to Farwah bint Abī Quḥāfah.
Abū ʿUbayd narrated it in (al-Amwāl (2)); perhaps her father had delegated the marriage to Abū Bakr.
ابن أبي خالد: عن قيس، قال:
When al-Ashʿath ibn Qays was brought as a captive to Abū Bakr, he released his bonds and married him to his sister.
He drew his sword and entered the camel market, and whenever he saw a she-camel or a male camel he hamstrung it, and the people cried out: Al-Ashʿath has disbelieved!
Then he threw down his sword and said: By Allah, I did not disbelieve; rather this man married me to his sister; and had we been in our own land, we would have had a wedding feast other than this one. People of Medina, slaughter and eat! And owners of camels, come and take their equivalent! ⟦2:39⟧
Narrated by: عبد المؤمن بن علي، عن عبد السلام بن حرب، عنه.
إسماعيل: عن قيس، قال:
I attended a funeral at which were al-Ashʿath and Jarīr; al-Ashʿath put Jarīr forward and said:
This man did not apostatize, but I apostatized (1).
Abū ʿUbaydah said: Al-Ashʿath was on the right wing of ʿAlī on the day of Ṣiffīn.
مسلمة بن محارب: عن حرب بن خالد بن يزيد بن معاوية، قال:
Muʿāwiyah mustered (2) ninety thousand and moved ahead, and camped at the Euphrates. ʿAlī came, and Muʿāwiyah denied them the water, so ʿAlī sent al-Ashʿath with two thousand (3), while at the water for Muʿāwiyah was Abū al-Aʿwar with five thousand; they fought fiercely, and al-Ashʿath prevailed over the water (4).
الأعمش: عن حيان أبي سعيد التيمي (5)، قال:
Al-Ashʿath was warned against the trials, and it was said to him: You went out with ʿAlī!
He said: And who do you have as a leader like ʿAlī (6)!
And from Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim, who said:
Al-Ashʿath went in to ʿAlī about some matter, and he threatened him with death.
ʿAlī said: Do you threaten me with death! I do not care about it. Bring me a collar ⟦2:40⟧ and a shackle!
Then he gestured to his companions.
He said: They pleaded with him on his behalf, and he let him go.
أبو المغيرة الخولاني: حدثنا صفوان بن عمرو؛ حدثني أبو الصلت الحضرمي، قال:
We stood between the people of Iraq and the water; then a horseman came to us and bared his face, and it was al-Ashʿath ibn Qays, and he said:
Allah, Allah, Muʿāwiyah, regarding the community of Muḥammad ﷺ! Suppose you killed the people of Iraq, who would be left for the expeditionary forces and the offspring? Or suppose we killed you, who would be left for the expeditionary forces and the offspring? Allah says: “And if two parties of the believers fight each other, then make peace between them” [Qurʾān 49:9].
Muʿāwiyah said: What do you want?
He said: Let us have access to the water.
So he said to Abū al-Aʿwar: Let our brothers have access to the water (1).
He narrated: الشيباني (2)، عن قيس بن محمد بن الأشعث:
that al-Ashʿath was governor for ʿUthmān over Adharbayjān, and once swore an oath about something, then expiated his oath with fifteen thousand.
إسماعيل بن أبي خالد: عن الشعبي، قال:
Al-Ashʿath had sworn an oath, and then said:
May Allah disfigure you, O wealth! By Allah, I swore only in truth, but it was returned to its owner, and it was thirty thousand.
شريك: حدثنا أبو إسحاق، قال:
I prayed the dawn prayer in the mosque of al-Ashʿath, and when the prayer leader gave the closing salutation, there was before me a purse and a sandal; I looked, and before every man was a purse and a sandal.
I said: What is this?
They said: Al-Ashʿath arrived tonight and said:
Look! ⟦2:41⟧
Everyone who prays the morning prayer in our mosque, put before him a purse and a pair of shoes.
Abū Isrāʾīl narrated it from Abū Isḥāq, except that he said: a robe and two sandals (1).
أحمد بن حنبل: حدثنا علي بن ثابت، حدثنا أبو المهاجر، عن ميمون بن مهران، قال:
The first man for whom men walked while he rode: al-Ashʿath ibn Qays.
Abū al-Malīḥ narrated something similar from Maymūn (2).
قال إسماعيل بن أبي خالد: عن حكيم بن جابر، قال:
When al-Ashʿath ibn Qays died, al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī came to them and ordered them to perform ablution on him with camphor, an ablution, and his daughter was married to al-Ḥasan (3).
They said: He died in the year 40.
Some added: Forty nights after ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him).
He was buried in his house.
It is said: he lived 63 years.
Muḥammad ibn Saʿd said: He died in Kufa, and al-Ḥasan was there at the time he made peace with Muʿāwiyah, and it was he who prayed over him.
I say: After him his son Muḥammad ibn al-Ashʿath was one of the great and noble commanders, ⟦2:42⟧ and he was the father of the commander ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ashʿath, with whom the people rose out, and who waged with al-Ḥajjāj those famous wars the like of which has not been heard of.
So that it is said: he waged eighty-one pitched battles with him (1), most of them against al-Ḥajjāj.
Then in the end Ibn al-Ashʿath was forsaken and routed, then they overcame him, and he perished.

104.h: 9 - Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿah ʿAmr ibn ʿUmayr ibn Salamah al-Lakhmī *
104.t:
The Meccan, ally of Banū Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Quṣayy.
One of the famous Emigrants; he witnessed Badr and the other battles.
He was the messenger of the Prophet ﷺ to al-Muqawqis, the ruler of Egypt.
He was a trader in foodstuffs, and had slaves.
He was one of the renowned archers.
Al-Ḥākim mentioned him in his (al-Mustadrak (2)), saying: He was of fine build, thin-bearded, stooped (3), tending toward shortness, thick-fingered.
Al-Wāqidī said this.
Hārūn ibn Yaḥyā al-Ḥāṭibī narrated, saying:
حدثني أبو ربيعة، عن عبد ⟦2:43⟧ الحميد بن أبي أنس، عن صفوان بن سليم، عن أنس، سمع حاطبا يقول:
He came upon the Prophet ﷺ at Uḥud. He said:
In ʿAlī's hand was the shield, and the Prophet ﷺ was washing his face with water.
Ḥāṭib said: Who did this?
ʿUtbah ibn Abī Waqqāṣ said: He smashed my face and broke my incisors with a stone!
I said: I heard a crier on the mountain: Muḥammad has been killed! So I came to you - as though my soul had departed - so where did ʿUtbah head?
He pointed to where he had headed.
I went on until I got hold of him, struck him with the sword, and threw down his head!
Then I dismounted, took his head, his spoils and his horse, and brought it to the Prophet ﷺ, who granted that to me and prayed for me, saying: (May Allah be pleased with you), twice (1).
A dark chain of transmission (الإسناد).
الليث: عن أبي الزبير، عن جابر: that a slave of Ḥāṭib complained about Ḥāṭib, saying:
O Prophet of Allah, he will surely enter the Fire!
He said: You have lied; he will never enter it, for he witnessed Badr and al-Ḥudaybiyah.
Authentic (صحيح) (2).
إسحاق بن راشد: عن الزهري، عن عروة، عن عبد الرحمن بن حاطب:
that his father wrote a letter to the disbelievers of Quraysh.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called ʿAlī and al-Zubayr and said: (Go until you overtake a woman carrying a letter, and bring it to me).
They met her and asked for the letter, and told her they would not turn back until they stripped off every garment she wore.
She said: Are you two not Muslims?
They said: Yes, but the Messenger of Allah told us that you have ⟦2:44⟧ a letter.
So she took it out from her hair.
He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called Ḥāṭib until the letter was read to him, and he acknowledged it.
He said: (What made you do it?).
He said: I had relatives and my child in Mecca, and I was a stranger among you, O company of Quraysh.
ʿUmar said: Permit me, O Messenger of Allah, to kill him.
He said: (No, he witnessed Badr, and you do not know, perhaps Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said: Do what you will, for I have forgiven you (1)).
Its chain of transmission (الإسناد) is fine, and its origin is in (the two Ṣaḥīḥs (الصحيحين) (2)).
Some of his clients (المولى) came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb complaining about him because of the expenditure on them; and he blamed him for it.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān his son was among those born in the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, and he saw him.
Narrating from him: ولده؛ الفقيه يحيى، وعروة بن الزبير، وغيرهما.
He died in the year 68.
Ḥāṭib died in the year 30. ⟦2:45⟧

107.h: 12 - ʿUmayr ibn Saʿd al-Anṣārī al-Awsī the ascetic (الزاهد) *
107.t:
Peerless.
He had a single hadith. ⟦2:103⟧
Narrating from him: أبو طلحة الخولاني، وراشد بن سعد، وحبيب بن عبيد.
He witnessed the conquest of Syria, and governed Damascus and Homs for ʿUmar.
A group: عن حماد بن سلمة، عن أبي سنان، عن أبي طلحة، قال:
We came to ʿUmayr ibn Saʿd - who was called: peerless (1) - and sat in his house, and he said: Boy, bring the horses to water.
He watered them, and he said: Where is so-and-so?
He said: Mangy, dripping blood.
He said: Water her; I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (There is no contagion, no bird omen, and no owl omen (2)).
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-Qaddāḥ said: ʿUmayr ibn Saʿd ibn Shuhayd accompanied the Prophet ﷺ and did not witness any of the battles.
It was he who reported to the Prophet ﷺ the words of al-Julās ibn Suwayd, who was an orphan in his care. ⟦2:104⟧
ʿUmar appointed him over Homs, and he was one of the ascetics (الزاهد).
ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn Saʿīd said: His governorship of Homs was after Ibn Ḥudhaym.
ابن لهيعة: عن يونس، عن الزهري، قال:
Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir died, and ʿUmayr ibn Saʿd took his place, and he was over Syria, he and Muʿāwiyah, until ʿUmar was killed.
And from Ibn Shihāb, who said: Then ʿUthmān gathered Syria for Muʿāwiyah and removed ʿUmayr.
وروى: عاصم بن عمر بن قتادة، عن عبد الرحمن بن عمير بن سعد:
Ibn ʿUmar said to me: There was no man among the Companions (الصحابي) of the Muslims better than your father (1).
وروى: هشام بن حسان، عن ابن سيرين، قال:
Out of ʿUmar's admiration for ʿUmayr ibn Saʿd he would call him: peerless, and once sent him over an army.
Al-Mufaḍḍal al-Ghallābī said: The ascetics (الزاهد) of the Anṣār are three: Abū al-Dardāʾ, Shaddād ibn Aws, and ʿUmayr ibn Saʿd.
Ibn ʿAsākir gave a full account of his reports (may Allah be pleased with him).

108.h: 13 - Abū Sufyān Ṣakhr ibn Ḥarb ibn Umayyah al-Umawī *
108.t:
Ibn ʿAbd Shams ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy ibn ⟦2:105⟧ Kilāb.
Chief of Quraysh and their commander on the day of Uḥud and the day of the Trench.
He had faults and grave matters, but Allah remedied him with Islam on the day of the Conquest, and he became Muslim as one compelled and afraid.
Then after some days his Islam became sound.
He was one of the shrewd men of the Arabs, and among the people of judgment and nobility among them; he witnessed Ḥunayn, and his son-in-law the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave him from the spoils a hundred camels and forty ounces of silver dirhams to win his heart thereby (1).
Then he turned away from worship of Hubal and inclined to Islam.
He witnessed the fighting at al-Ṭāʾif, where his eye was gouged out, then the other was gouged out on the day of al-Yarmūk; by that day - Allah willing - his faith had become good, for that day he was urging jihad.
He was under the banner of his son Yazīd, and kept crying out: O help of Allah, draw near (2).
He would stand over the squadrons (3) reminding, and saying:
Allah, Allah! You are the helpers of Islam and the core (4) of the Arabs, and these are the helpers of polytheism and the core of the Romans; O Allah, this is one of Your days, O Allah, send down Your help. ⟦2:106⟧
If this is authentic from him, he is to be envied for it.
There is no doubt that his account about Heraclius (1) and the letter of the Prophet ﷺ indicates his faith, and praise be to Allah.
He was ten years older than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He lived twenty years after him.
ʿUmar respected him; that was because he was the elder of Banū Umayyah.
He was the father-in-law of the Prophet ﷺ.
He did not die until he saw his two sons Yazīd and then Muʿāwiyah as governors of Damascus.
He loved leadership and renown, and had great prestige (2) during the caliphate (الخلافة) of his cousin ʿUthmān.
He died in Medina in the year 31.
It is said: in the year 32.
It is said: in the year 33 or 34, aged about 90.

109.h: 14 - al-Ḥakam ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ ibn Umayyah al-Umawī Abū Marwān *
109.t:
Cousin of Abū Sufyān.
He was given the patronymic (الكنية): Abū Marwān.
He was among those who became Muslim at the Conquest, and had the least share of companionship. ⟦2:107⟧
It is said: the Prophet ﷺ banished him to al-Ṭāʾif because he mimicked him in his walk and some of his movements; so he cursed him and expelled him, and he settled in the valley of Wajj (1).
A group resented the Commander of the Faithful (أمير المؤمنين) ʿUthmān for being kind to his uncle al-Ḥakam, sheltering him, bringing him to Medina and giving him a hundred thousand.
Hadiths are reported in censure of him that did not prove authentic (2).
And from the Prophet ﷺ: (What is it that I was shown the sons of al-Ḥakam leaping on my pulpit like the leaping of monkeys (3)!).
Narrated by: العلاء بن عبد الرحمن، عن أبيه، عن أبي هريرة.
There are hadiths on this subject.
Al-Shaʿbī said: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr say:
By the Lord of this Kaʿbah, al-Ḥakam ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ and his offspring are cursed on the tongue of Muḥammad ﷺ.
Al-Ḥakam had twenty sons and eight daughters.
It is said: he used to divulge the secret of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he removed him for that.
He died in the year 31. ⟦2:108⟧

110.h: 15 - Kisrā Yazdajird ibn Shahriyār ibn Parwīz *
110.t:
The last of the Khosraus without qualification.
His name was: Yazdajird ibn Shahriyār ibn Parwīz, the Zoroastrian, the Persian.
He fled from the army of ʿUmar, and they took control of Iraq, and he fled to Merv; his days passed, then the commanders of his state rose against him and killed him in the year 30.
It is said: rather the Turks attacked him by night and killed his close associates, and he fled and hid in a house, and the owner of the house betrayed him and killed him, and then they killed him for it (1).

111.h: 16 - Khadījah bint Khuwaylid ibn Asad al-Asadiyyah, Mother of the Believers **
111.t:
And the mistress of the women of the worlds in her time.
Umm al-Qāsim, daughter of Khuwaylid ibn Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Quṣayy ibn Kilāb al-Qurashiyyah, al-Asadiyyah.
Mother of the children of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the first to believe in him, and she believed him before anyone, steadied his heart, and went with him to her cousin Waraqah (2). ⟦2:109⟧
Her virtues are many.
She was among those women who attained perfection: intelligent, dignified, devout, chaste, generous, of the people of Paradise; the Prophet ﷺ would praise her, prefer her over all the other Mothers of the Believers, and go to great lengths in honouring her, such that ʿĀʾishah used to say:
I was never jealous of any woman as I was jealous of Khadījah, from how often the Prophet ﷺ mentioned her (1).
Among her honour with him ﷺ: that he married no woman before her, and several children came to him from her, and he never married another over her, nor took a concubine, until she met her end; and he felt her loss, for she was an excellent companion.
She spent on him from her wealth, and he ﷺ traded for her.
Allah commanded him to give her glad tidings of a house in Paradise of hollowed pearl, with no noise and no toil in it (2).
الواقدي: حدثنا ابن أبي حبيبة، عن داود بن الحصين، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، وابن أبي الزناد، عن هشام، وروي عن جبير بن مطعم:
that Khadījah's uncle ʿAmr ibn Asad married her to the Prophet ﷺ, and that her father had died before ⟦2:110⟧ the Fijār (1).
Then al-Wāqidī said: This is what our colleagues agree on, with no disagreement among them (2).
الكلبي: عن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس:
that the Prophet ﷺ married her when she was twenty-eight years old (3).
Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār said: In the Jāhiliyyah (الجاهلية) Khadījah was called al-Ṭāhirah.
Her mother was: Fāṭimah bint Zāʾidah al-ʿĀmiriyyah.
Khadījah was first married to Abū Hālah ibn Zurārah al-Tamīmī, then after him ʿAtīq ibn ʿĀbid (4) ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn Makhzūm succeeded him with her, then after him the Prophet ﷺ, who consummated the marriage with her when he was twenty-five.
She was fifteen years older than him.
From ʿĀʾishah: that Khadījah died before the prayer was made obligatory.
It is said: she died ⟦2:111⟧ in Ramadan and was buried at al-Ḥajūn (1), aged 65.
وقال مروان بن معاوية، عن وائل بن داود، عن عبد الله البهي، قال:
ʿĀʾishah said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned Khadījah, he would hardly tire of praising her and asking forgiveness for her.
One day he mentioned her, and jealousy carried me away, and I said: Allah has compensated you with one advanced in age!
He said: I saw him become angry with such anger that I was thrown into confusion in my mind (2), and I said to myself:
O Allah, if You remove the anger of Your messenger from me, I will never again mention her ill.
When the Prophet ﷺ saw what I had met with, he said: (What did you say? By Allah, she believed in me when the people denied me, sheltered me when the people rejected me, and I was granted children from her, while you were deprived of them through me).
She said: And for a month he went out morning and evening speaking of her to me (3).
Al-Wāqidī said: They came out of the Shiʿb of Banū Hāshim three years before the Hijrah, and Abū Ṭālib died, and before him Khadījah by a month and five days.
Al-Ḥākim said: She died three days after Abū Ṭālib.
هشام بن عروة: عن أبيه، عن عائشة:
I was never jealous of any woman as I was jealous of Khadījah, because of what I heard of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ's mention of her, and he married me only three years after her death.
And his Lord had commanded him to give her glad tidings of a house in Paradise of hollowed pearl (4). ⟦2:112⟧
Abū Yaʿlā in his (Musnad), by our direct hearing (السماع): حدثنا إسحاق بن أبي إسرائيل، حدثنا سهل بن زياد - reliable (ثقة) - حدثني الأزرق بن قيس، عن عبد الله بن نوفل - أو ابن بريدة - عن خديجة بنت خويلد، قالت:
I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Where are my children by you?
He said: (In Paradise).
She said: And where are my children by my husbands among the polytheists?
He said: (In the Fire).
I said: Without any deed?
He said: (Allah knows best what they would have done (1)).
There is a disconnection (المنقطع) in it.
محمد بن فضيل: عن عمارة، عن أبي زرعة، سمع أبا هريرة يقول:
Gabriel came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: Here is Khadījah coming to you with a vessel containing seasoning or food or drink; when she comes to you, convey to her greetings of peace from her Lord and from me, and give her glad tidings of a house in Paradise of hollowed pearl, with no noise and no toil.
Agreed upon (المتفق عليه) as to its authenticity (2).
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (The best of her women is Khadījah bint Khuwaylid, and the best of her women is Maryam bint ʿImrān (3)).
أحمد: حدثنا محمد بن بشر، حدثنا محمد بن عمرو، حدثنا أبو سلمة، ويحيى بن عبد الرحمن، قالا:
When Khadījah died, Khawlah bint Ḥakīm, wife of ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn, came and said: O Messenger of Allah, will you not marry? He said: ⟦2:113⟧
(Whom?).
She said: Sawdah bint Zamʿah, who believed in you and followed you ... , the hadith in full (1), and it is mursal (مرسل).
Ibn Isḥāq said: Calamities came one after another upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with the deaths of Abū Ṭālib and Khadījah.
Khadījah was a vizier of truth (2).
She was closer to Quṣayy than the Prophet ﷺ by one man.
She was wealthy, and she proposed to the Prophet ﷺ that he go out with her wealth to Syria, so he went out with her client (المولى) Maysarah.
When he returned, Khadījah sold what he had brought, and it multiplied, so she desired him, and offered herself to him, and he married her, and gave her a dower of twenty young camels.
Her children by him: al-Qāsim, al-Ṭayyib and al-Ṭāhir, who died as infants; and Ruqayyah, Zaynab, Umm Kulthūm and Fāṭimah (3).
ʿĀʾishah said: The first thing with which the revelation to the Prophet ﷺ began was the true dream ... , until she said:
Then he said: “Read in the name of your Lord who created” (Qurʾān 96:1).
She said: He returned with it, his shoulder muscles trembling (4), until he entered upon Khadījah and said: (Cover me).
They covered him until the fear left him, and he said: (What is wrong with me, Khadījah?).
And he told her the matter, and said: (I fear for myself).
She said to him: Never, rejoice, for by Allah, Allah will never disgrace you (5) ⟦2:114⟧ ever; you maintain ties of kinship, speak the truth, bear burdens, and help in the misfortunes of the right.
And she went with him to her cousin Waraqah ibn Nawfal ibn Asad, a man who had become Christian in the Jāhiliyyah (الجاهلية), who used to write Arabic script, and wrote from the Gospel in Arabic what Allah willed him to write, and who was an old man who had gone blind.
She said: Listen to your nephew, what he says.
He said: O son of my brother, what do you see?
So he told him.
He said: This is the Nāmūs that was sent down upon Moses ... , the hadith (1).
Shaykh ʿIzz al-Dīn ibn al-Athīr said: Khadījah was the first of Allah's creation to become Muslim, by the consensus (الإجماع) of the Muslims (2).
Al-Zuhrī, Qatādah, Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, Ibn Isḥāq, al-Wāqidī, and Saʿīd ibn Yaḥyā said:
The first to believe in Allah and His Messenger were Khadījah, Abū Bakr, and ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with them). ⟦2:115⟧
Ibn Isḥāq said: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ḥakīm narrated to me:
that it reached him from Khadījah that she said: O cousin, can you tell me of your companion when he comes to you?
When he came, he said: (Khadījah, this is Gabriel).
She said: Sit on my thigh.
He did so, and she said: Do you see him?
He said: (Yes).
She said: Then move to the left thigh.
He did so, she said: Do you see him?
He said: (Yes).
She threw off her veil and bared her chest, and said: Do you see him?
He said: (No).
She said: Rejoice, for he is - by Allah - an angel, and not a devil (1).
Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: It is reported through several routes:
that the Prophet ﷺ said: (Khadījah, Gabriel conveys greetings of peace to you).
And in some: O Muḥammad, convey to Khadījah greetings of peace from her Lord (2).
From Ḥudhayfah: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Khadījah is the foremost of the women of the worlds in belief in Allah and in Muḥammad (3) ﷺ).
There is softness (لين الحديث) in its chain of transmission (الإسناد).
حماد بن سلمة: عن حميد، عن عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير، قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ grieved for Khadījah until it was feared for him, until he married ʿĀʾishah (4).
معمر: عن قتادة، وأبو جعفر الرازي، عن ثابت، واللفظ لقتادة، عن ⟦2:116⟧ أنس مرفوعا: (Enough for you of the women of the worlds are four (1)).
Thābit said: from Anas: (The best of the women of the worlds: Maryam, Āsiyah, Khadījah bint Khuwaylid, and Fāṭimah (2)).
الدراوردي: عن إبراهيم بن عقبة، عن كريب، عن ابن عباس:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (The mistress of the women of the people of Paradise after Maryam: Fāṭimah, Khadījah, and the wife of Pharaoh, Āsiyah (3)).
مجالد: عن الشعبي، عن مسروق، عن عائشة، قالت:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned Khadījah, and I spoke ill of her, and said:
An old woman! such and such; Allah has replaced her for you with better than her.
He said: (Allah has not replaced her for me with better; she believed in me when people disbelieved, shared with me her wealth when people deprived me, and Allah granted me her children and deprived me of the children of others).
I said: By Allah, I will not reproach you about her after today (4).
وروى: عروة، عن عائشة، قالت: Khadījah died before the prayer was made obligatory.
Al-Wāqidī said: She died in Ramadan and was buried at al-Ḥajūn.
Qatādah said: She died three years before the Hijrah.
ʿUrwah said the same. ⟦2:117⟧

112.h: 17 - Fāṭimah bint Asad ibn Hāshim ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy al-Hāshimiyyah *
112.t:
Mother of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib.
She is the mother-in-law of Fāṭimah; she was among the first Emigrant women, and the first Hāshimite woman to give birth to a Hāshimite.
Al-Zubayr said this.
Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said:
وروى: سعدان بن الوليد السابري، عن عطاء، عن ابن عباس، قال:
When Fāṭimah, the mother of ʿAlī, died, the Prophet ﷺ clothed her in his shirt and lay down with her in her grave.
They said: We have not seen you do this, O Messenger of Allah!
He said: (After Abū Ṭālib no one was more dutiful to me than she; I clothed her in my shirt only so that she be clothed in the garments of Paradise, and lay with her only to ease it for her).
This is gharīb (الغريب) (1).
